item.description: Watch as Nick Sirianni approaches fans, needs guided back to field following win over Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . At this point, most NFL fans are familiar with Nick Sirianni's style of celebrating. The Eagles head coach has had many moments over the last few years in which he's rubbed opposing fanbases the wrong way by getting a bit too fired up on the sideline, trash-talking with fans and more. So of course, after Philadelphia stunned Dallas on Thanksgiving, Sirianni had something to say about it. In the moments after Joe Milton, Devonta Smith and Jake Elliott led the Eagles to a historic comeback win, Sirianni had to be guided back toward the field by "Big Dom" and more Eagles staffers after celebrating in the area of fans. Here's a look at the viral moment of Sirianni celebrating after the Eagles' win. MORE: How Joe Milton may have secured next contract with performance vs. Cowboys Nick Sirianni approaches fans following Eagles win over Cowboys Not long after Elliott's long-range field goal won it for the Eagles, Sirianni made his way over to an area full of Eagles fans, yelling in their direction and clearly fired up for the comeback. Eagles' chief security officer "Big Dom" was among the staffers who held Sirianni back and attempted to guide him back toward the field so he could go shake hands with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. #Eagles HC Nick Sirianni ended up by the stands with fans at the end of the game and had to be brought back to the field. https://t.co/3EFV2f6txi — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 Here's another angle of Sirianni approaching fans, which mostly appeared celebratory with Philadelphia fans: Nick Sirianni was fired up after one of the best comebacks in Eagles history against their biggest rival in Dallas https://t.co/PgDTrsRio4 — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) November 27, 2026 Sirianni also yelled "That's how you fight" as he walked back to the locker room: Nick Sirianni fired up after that win. https://t.co/fAbwKLZo70 — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) November 27, 2026 While the head coach didn't appear to violate any NFL protocols, it was the latest viral exchange in a growing history of Sirianni's personal exchanges with fans, heated moments with players and more. The pair grew up training side by side, sharing an ambitious goal of representing Canada in wrestling at the Olympic Games. Anastasia went on to earn podium finishes at the Ontario Federation of School Athletic Associations championships in 2007 and 2008. She recalled their early aspirations: “Before fighting, we wanted to be like on the Olympic team for wrestling. So that was our aspirations, to be on the Olympic team for Canada.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Over time, their paths naturally diverged. Once a training camp begins, however, a much more serious persona takes over. The Canadian becomes fiercely protective of her focus, often limiting outside contact and trusting her coaches to handle the film study on her opponents. She explained: “I love training. item.title: Five Levski fans taken to hospital as presidents condemn Marseille violence
item.description: Marseille police said 11 people were injured in the clashes, all of them Bulgarian (Justine MEDDAH) Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans. The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said it was "unacceptable" and "shocking". "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said. Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered. Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said. - 'Violent times' - "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Iotova said: "The French authorities must clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them, and UEFA should check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured. "We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf/cms/pst

item.title: Eagles Security Forced to Step In as Nick Sirianni Appears to Confront Cowboys Fans After Historic Thanksgiving Win
item.description: Nick Sirianni ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Philadelphia Eagles seem to have finally caught a break this season. With a thrilling end to the Dallas Cowboys game on Thursday, head coach Nick Sirianni has plenty of reasons to celebrate. However, he might have gotten a bit too excited. As seen in the clips , doing rounds on social media, Sirianni is captured heading straight towards the Dallas fans with an agitated look after the win. Philadelphia’s chief security officer Domenico DiSandro, aka Big Dom, rushed to the scene to pull the head coach away from the crowd. Sirianni tried to charge back in. The heated rivalry between the two sides had the heat turned up with Sirianni celebrating the victory right in front of the home crowd. The Eagles head coach was so amped up after the win that he only gave a side hug to Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer, as part of the customary gesture after games. He didn’t even spare the losing coach a second glance and walked away right after. When a head coach's emotions boil over on the biggest stage, it reveals the intensity behind a dominant performance. Stay subscribed for the untold stories shaping the NFL's fiercest rivalries. What initially looked like a comfortable Cowboys victory turned into a stunning Eagles comeback, with Dallas surrendering a 31-10 lead before falling 39-38. Jake Elliott delivered the decisive blow with a 59-yard field goal with just two seconds remaining. The 21-point comeback was the largest ever in Thanksgiving game history for the NFL. The comeback was also made possible by an outstanding performance from Joe Milton, who delivered the best outing of his career. The Eagles quarterback threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing score. In the fourth quarter alone, Philadelphia added 22 points. Dallas tried to stay in the fight with a crazy touchdown from Dak Prescott, who was briefly in the air but managed to hang on to the ball for the score. However, it was all in vain, as Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal later on. This is not the first time that Big Dom had to step up and calm Sirianni down. Back in 2024, the Eagles head coach got into a heated fight with Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz as they shook hands after the game. Even though the Eagles wrote one of the best comeback wins on Thanksgiving, the head coach’s reaction did not sit well with many. “Nick Sirianni is classless and should not be an NFL head coach,” Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on X. “Buddy needs a nap and an ice cream sandwich to go chill out.” Walking back into the stadium after the game, that energy was still present in Sirianni. “We know how to fight,” he can be heard saying as he walks past the media. He also celebrated with Eagles fans nearby before he walked back in, high-fiving them. It all came about in a matter of minutes for Philadelphia, who were on a seven-game losing streak not long ago. Sirianni has reason to celebrate, but he sure will be asked about his behavior with the fans

item.title: Tom Brady rips into Aaron Rodgers for breaking ‘the sanctity of an NFL locker room’
item.description: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments. This time it was Tom Brady, who kept it professional but made clear that Rodgers’ takedown of the Steelers after his benching needed to stay in house. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast of the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys on Nov. 15, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. The Steelers cut Rodgers soon after the appearance on “McAfee,” and he cleared waivers Thursday to become a free agent. item.title: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles
item.description: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jerry Jones is more accessible than most NFL owners, to the point that he reliably speaks with the media after each game. For Cowboys fans, that's a blessing and a curse; they get to hear an immediate response from the owner, but the words aren't always what they want to hear. After Dallas inexplicably blew a 21-point lead to the division-rival Eagles on Thursday, Jones was blunt about the shocking defeat but didn't offer much in the way of potential changes. Here's a look at what Jones had to say. MORE: Joe Milton likely secured NFL future with win over Cowboys Jerry Jones responds to Cowboys' collapse Jones called the loss to the Eagles "numbing" but said he "wouldn't anticipate" coaching changes despite the long layoff before the Cowboys' next game. "We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time," Jones said. That came with a caveat, though. Jones said "nothing we've seen out here tonight" gives him confidence in coach Brian Schottenheimer, but he added, "You've got to look at everything," noting that there are "several more games to go." Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 As for the game itself, Jones was clear that everyone on the team, from himself to the players, shared responsibility. "It was ours to take, and we didn't," Jones said. "You have to question everything." QB Dak Prescott agreed with Jones' assessment of the loss. Told that Jones called the defeat "numbing," Prescott told reporters, "That's a good description for how I'm feeling right now." The Cowboys have yet to win back-to-back games this season, and they now trail the Giants by four games in the loss column. Jones typically resists coaching changes as long as possible, but the questions surrounding Schottenheimer aren't likely to fade anytime soon after a Thanksgiving collapse. item.title: Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. injury upgrade is good news for pivotal Raiders clash
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. injury upgrade is good news for pivotal Raiders clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns received an encouraging update on Harold Fannin Jr. ahead of their Sunday Night Football showdown with the Las Vegas Raiders. Fannin, who is dealing with a groin injury, was listed as a full participant on Thursday’s injury report after being limited on Wednesday. There is a catch, though. The Browns only held a walkthrough on Thursday, so the participation levels were estimates, according to Scott Petrak. Still, the upgrade is a positive sign for Cleveland’s top pass-catching threat. It’s also not the first time the groin issue has popped up for Fannin. He was limited with the same injury earlier this month heading into the Browns’ Week 9 matchup with the New Orleans Saints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He suited up in that game and nearly delivered a memorable win. In the closing minute of overtime, Fannin hauled in a pass, broke two tackles and raced into the end zone. Cleveland’s two-point try failed, however, and the Saints escaped with a 23-22 victory . The second-year tight end has been a reliable weapon this season . He entered the Browns’ Week 10 matchup with the Houston Texans with 453 receiving yards and four touchdowns, and he followed it up with another impactful outing in Cleveland’s 27-24 win. His availability is especially important given what’s at stake. The Browns sit at 6-4 and are fresh off their bye week, putting them right in the thick of the AFC playoff race. A win over the 4-7 Raiders at home would keep them in the hunt in a crowded AFC North . Fannin wasn’t the only tight end to get good news. Blake Whiteheart was also upgraded from limited to full with a hip injury, while rookie guard Austin Barber went from not practicing to limited with a knee issue. On the other hand, defensive ends Derek Barnett and Isaiah McGuire, along with rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston, did not participate for a second straight day. Cleveland’s final injury report is due on Friday. item.title: Bears’ Jeffery Simmons calls out Lions for ‘crying’ over Juice Scruggs’ false starts
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Jeffery Simmons calls out Lions for ‘crying’ over Juice Scruggs’ false starts appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Just when the Detroit Lions appeared to have the showdown wrapped up, the Chicago Bears pulled off a wild comeback to secure the victory, 39-35, on Rome Odunze’s six-yard touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears stunned the Lions at Ford Field , erasing an 11-point deficit in the fourth quarter for their sixth straight win and solo possession of the top spot in the NFC North. Plenty of gamesmanship happened, including Jeffery Simmons causing Juice Scruggs to commit a false start three times. When asked about it, Simmons stressed that it was not illegal . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s a lot of crying on that side of the ball when that happened,” said the three-time All-Pro in the video posted by CHGO Bears. “When Jared (Goff) checked, I said, ‘It’s a run.’ It’s not my fault that your center jumped. That’s literally the only time I said something. All the other ones, I think he just knew when I was lined up to the right of his head. That’s on him. He tried to get into position so he could block me, just like the one he fumbled. He saw me, and I’m firing off the ball, but at the end of the day, I don’t have to cheat.” Jeffery Simmons on Lions C Juice Scruggs’ multiple false starts during Thanksgiving matchup: pic.twitter.com/wfRYS3zwOn — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) November 26, 2026 The 27-year-old Simmons logged three tackles. Chicago improved to 9-2, including 4-1 on the road. “You’re gonna get a lot of complaining when you lose a football game, when you get a false start. But it is what it is,” added the four-time Pro Bowler. He has yet to lose with the Bears since being acquired in a trade with the Tennessee Titans in exchange for draft capital in October. The Bears will host the Jacksonville Jaguars on December 6. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Addresses Jeffery Simmons’ Actions Goff’s comments came on the same day that Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany accused the Bears of simulating Detroit’s snap count and suggested that the NFL could investigate audio recordings from the game. Goff took a more measured approach, acknowledging how difficult it can be for officials to determine a defensive player’s intentions. “I only think he did it really once that was really egregious to me, where they yell,” Goff said. “It’s a really hard thing to officiate because at what point is he simulating the snap count? At what point is he just talking to his guys? “I understand it happens all across the league. It isn’t the first time it’s happened. “But I’m just trying to make sure that they know that I’m not allowed to simulate snap count with my hands. He shouldn’t be allowed to do it with his voice. “That wasn’t the difference in the game, but that was early, and I don’t believe it happened more than once or twice.” As reported by the Detroit Free Press via Yahoo Sports , Simmons denied mimicking Detroit’s snap count following the game. Goff’s comments suggest that while he was frustrated by what occurred, he recognizes there is a fine line between defensive communication and intentionally disrupting offensive signals. Jared Goff Does Not Want Controversy Overblown Later in his press conference, Goff returned to the subject and reiterated that the alleged snap-count simulation was not responsible for Detroit’s Thanksgiving Day loss. Instead, he placed the responsibility on himself and his teammates to handle those situations better. “I don’t think that should be overblown. I think it happened a couple times, and the officials talked to them,” Goff said. “If they were trying to simulate the snap count or if they weren’t, I don’t know. They could probably say they aren’t, and it’s impossible to officiate, and they’ll never throw a flag on it. “This isn’t the first game that’s happened. We’ve got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.” Goff’s response is consistent with what Dan Campbell recently revealed about his quarterback’s resilience and competitive mentality . Rather than pointing fingers following a frustrating loss, Goff acknowledged that Detroit needs to be better prepared to handle those situations. Detroit Lions Had Opportunities to Put Bears Away While the snap-count controversy will understandably generate plenty of discussion, the Lions had more than enough opportunities to win Thursday’s game. According to the official Lions game recap , Detroit held a 35-24 fourth-quarter lead before allowing Chicago to score 15 unanswered points. Instead of extending their winning streak to seven games and reversing a historical trend dating back to 1934 , the Lions fell to 8-3 and surrendered first place in the NFC North to the Bears. Whether the NFL eventually examines the allegations raised by Mahogany remains to be seen. As for Goff, his message was clear: Regardless of what Simmons was doing at the line of scrimmage, the Lions had opportunities to win the game and failed to capitalize on them.

item.title: ‘Is This How You Want To Go Out?’ — Russell Wilson Makes Feelings Clear on Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Steelers Exit After Feud With Mike McCarthy
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers turned the Pittsburgh Steelers’ world upside down on Wednesday, airing a ton of dirty laundry regarding his relationship with head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh sided with McCarthy by releasing Rodgers on Wednesday. This situation is still working itself out, with Rodgers clearing waivers, and much is being said about how the abrupt parting of ways has somewhat overshadowed the Thanksgiving slate of games. Many of Rodgers’ peers jumped into the conversation on Wednesday, and that trend continued on Thursday, with Russell Wilson also stepping into the discussion. Russell Wilson Criticizes Aaron Rodgers Over Steelers Fallout Seattle Seahawks legend Russell Wilson was on CBS’ pregame coverage of the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears game on Thursday. During that program, Wilson provided his thoughts on Rodgers and his messy situation with the Steelers. “We’ve all been in the room. Like, we’ve seen coaches fall asleep in moments, long days, long hours. We’ve seen players fall asleep in moments…. The reality is Aaron Rodgers wanted to call the plays, right? And that’s the difference here…. The reality is the ultimatum was the ultimatum,” Wilson said . “If not, I want my release, essentially. And so they made that decision…. It’s about Aaron Rodgers’ legacy…. If I’m his family members, if I’m somebody close to him, I’m his significant other, whatever it may be: ‘Is this how you want to go out?’ After all the success he’s had, is this how you want to go out?… This is a disappointment,” Wilson added. Rodgers played for the Steelers last season prior to McCarthy’s hiring. The future Hall of Fame quarterback mentioned on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday that he vouched for McCarthy to be interviewed for the Pittsburgh job following the 2025 campaign. It was a bit of a mystery as to whether Rodgers would return for 2026. However, he elected to give it one final go and signed a one-year contract to return to Pittsburgh. Pittsburgh was winning games, at the very least, and was in the running in the AFC North. However, Pittsburgh has lost its last two games. As a result, the team felt like it needed to spark a change somehow, opting to bench Rodgers and start Mason Rudolph in Week 12 against the Denver Broncos. Things went off the rails when Rodgers appeared on McAfee’s show on Wednesday. He accused McCarthy of various things, such as sleeping through meetings, missing team activities, and breaking the team down by invoking the Green Bay Packers during halftime of a recent game. The fallout continues to reverberate through the NFL, with even Tom Brady weighing in on Thursday night. item.title: Liga record setter Simeone's Atletico in pursuit of top two
item.description: Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone boasts more victories than any other manager in La Liga history (Javier SORIANO) No coach in the history of Spanish football has won more La Liga matches than Atletico Madrid's Diego Simeone. The Argentine claimed his 345th league victory last weekend to keep the Rojiblancos in the race to chase down Spain's traditional giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid. Third-placed Atletico visit Elche on Saturday with Simeone looking to keep adding to his record and deliver a third La Liga title, adding to his conquests in 2014 and 2021. Atletico trail leaders Barcelona by five points before they face the Catalans on December 2, in a match brought forward because of the teams' participation in the Spanish Super Cup in January. Barcelona visit Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday, while Real Madrid, second and two points ahead of Atletico, host Alaves on Saturday. Simeone surpassed the late Luis Aragones, on 344 league victories, to stand alone at the top of the all-time list. "I would like to share this number with all the people behind these 345 victories," said Simeone, speaking of his family, current and former staff and players. "I don't usually get excited about many things, but getting to this point has taken incredible work." Prying two league titles away from giants Real Madrid and Barcelona was an impressive achievement, and Atletico have shown this season they have the tools to do it again. Until their defeat by Barcelona before the international break, Atletico won their seven prior league matches, including a derby victory over Real Madrid. Their strong start has come without star player Julian Alvarez being at his best, which shows they can still find a higher gear. The Argentine forward wanted to leave in the summer and tried to force through a move to Barcelona, but Atletico staunchly resisted. Alvarez started the season at a low ebb and struggling for fitness, and has scored just three goals across all competitions to date. However the 2022 World Cup winner has started to show some of his quality in recent appearances and tensions with the supporters have eased. - 'Same ambition, hunger - Alvarez set up Atletico's first two goals against Getafe in their win last weekend and scored with a free-kick against Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. "He's truly an incredible player, fantastic. I like him as a person, I'll support him as a footballer, I understand him as a player," said Simeone on Wednesday. "Even though he hasn't scored in previous matches, there isn't an attacking move that doesn't go through him, and he always contributes important things. To get where we want to be, we need the best Julian Alvarez." Simeone's other two title successes were powered by goals from South American strikers, with Brazilian Diego Costa key in 2014, and Uruguay's Luis Suarez vital in 2021. item.title: Bayern risk more than sporting success as Musiala saga rolls on
item.description: Jamal Musiala signals to the bench with injury. (Alexandra BEIER) Bayern Munich head to Hamburg on Saturday in the middle of a crisis which threatens not only to derail the club's sporting ambitions, but their identity itself. Bayern, who are in the midst of an injury crisis which has decimated their forward line including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, sit two points behind Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga table. But Bayern's treatment of midfielder Jamal Musiala by their hierarchy has led to a growing rift between the club and the playing group. Shortly after Bayern lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday, ending their run as the final unbeaten team in Europe's top-five leagues this season, vice-captain Joshua Kimmich suggested the club had fallen out of step with their values. "It's completely unacceptable and is not Bayern-like," Kimmich said on Wednesday, adding that Musiala's treatment was inconsistent with the club's "sense of togetherness". - 'Mia san mia' - This week, Bayern's hierarchy suggested Musiala take a pay cut as the 23-year-old battles his way back from a neurological condition which causes absence seizures. While the condemnation from media, player unions and former players was swift, Kimmich -- who was wearing the captain's armband with Manuel Neuer out injured -- was the first member of Bayern's current squad to speak out. Despite their status as one of football's perennial heavyweights, Bayern have always sought to emphasise their Bavarian roots and member-ownership in contrast to the American and Gulf-owned behemoths that loom over the European landscape. But their cold-hearted treatment of Musiala, a fan-favourite and popular inside the dressing room, threatens their carefully crafted identity. The club's vaunted 'Mia san mia' motto, which appears on every modern Bayern kit, translates to 'we are who we are'. item.title: Verstappen spells out what truly puts him off racing in the Indy 500
item.description: Max Verstappen has revealed why he is unwilling to take part in the Indianapolis 500, citing the risks associated with oval racing and the serious accident suffered by Nelson Piquet at Indianapolis. The four-time Formula 1 world champion has made no secret of his ambitions to compete in other motorsport disciplines alongside his commitments with Red Bull Racing, with endurance racing among the Dutchman's main interests. However, despite his admiration for the Indianapolis 500, Verstappen is not particularly interested in testing himself at the prestigious American event. The Red Bull driver explained that his reluctance has nothing to do with doubts over his ability to be competitive, but rather with the risks involved. Verstappen cites Piquet's Indianapolis crash Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Verstappen pointed to the accident suffered by three-time F1 world champion Piquet, the father of his partner Kelly, as one of the reasons behind his stance. The Brazilian suffered serious injuries to both legs and feet during practice for the 1992 Indianapolis 500, requiring extensive surgery and months of rehabilitation. Despite the severity of his injuries, Piquet returned to Indianapolis the following year and qualified for the race. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen stressed that witnessing the long-term consequences of Piquet's accident has influenced his attitude towards competing in the American showpiece. "It's not that I think I won't be good at it. It's just the risk management. That's why I don't want to do it," Verstappen explained. "I like watching it, but I also know there is a very high risk involved by crashing, and I have had plenty of examples. "Even, of course, my father-in-law had a big crash there. And seeing how he had to live for the rest of his life after that crash is some risk that I'm not willing to take while already doing F1 and racing in GT3." The Dutchman also explained that, given the risks he already exposes himself to through his commitments in both Formula 1 and GT3 racing, he sees little reason to add another potentially dangerous undertaking to his schedule. "At one point, you're taking already a lot of risk. So sometimes then it's good to also have a few weekends where you don't need to be on the limit all the time."

item.title: UConn Men's Basketball: Dan Hurley Addresses Future of Huskies-Duke Rivalry
item.description:
The UConn Huskies men's basketball team suffered its second consecutive loss on Wednesday night, dropping a neutral site contest against the Duke Blue Devils. With the loss, the Huskies are now 4-2 on the season, having also lost to Arizona last Wednesday. While UConn still remains as one of the best teams in the country, especially with Solo Ball returning to the lineup, it is clearly trying to figure out how to play without Nik Khamenia, who is out with injury. The UConn-Duke showdown, played in Las Vegas, was one of the most highly-anticipated games of the college hoops season, but UConn head coach Dan Hurley seems to want it played in a different setting moving forward. The announced crowd of 8,500 was clearly good, but Hurley said afterwards that maybe the game would do better if it were a home-and-home series involving trips to Durham, N.C. and Storrs, Conn. He even mentioned the idea of playing the game at Madison Square Garden, suggesting that that venue would be better equipped to sell the game out. What would a home-and-home series mean for the rivalry? Simply put? It would be electric for the fans of both programs. The most fun college games are played on individual campuses or at campus-adjacent team arenas, but who knows if that can actually happen. Often times, neutral site games are worth more money to television networks, so maybe a game at Madison Square Garden is more logical. UConn is playing a ridiculously hard non-conference schedule this season, but only the game against Kansas on Dec. 12 is being played on camps at Gampel Pavilion. UConn Huskies head coach Dan Hurley talks to the referee during the first half against the Arizona Wildcats at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images
What's next for this UConn team? The Huskies are back in action on Monday night against Rider as they ease back into the non-conference schedule after the Thanksgiving holiday. And how about the rest of UConn Athletics? 1) Well, the UConn football team will close out the regular season on Saturday afternoon (noon ET) against Wyoming. The Huskies are 6-5 while the Cowboys are 7-4. UConn is already bowl-eligible, but it isn't guaranteed a bowl game berth at this time. Winning a seventh game on the season would go a long way toward guaranteeing that. 2) The UConn women's basketball team will take on No. 5 Duke on Saturday night at 7 p.m. ET. The Blue Devils are coached by Kara Lawson, who helped lead Team USA to a FIBA World Cup gold medal this summer.

item.title: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to address Aaron Rodgers' exit: Live updates
item.description: It may be Thanksgiving. It may be a day removed from Aaron Rodgers' stunning divorce from the Pittsburgh Steelers , who will host the Denver Broncos for the league's now-annual Black Friday game. But the four-time NFL MVP and, suddenly, NFL free agent remains at the forefront of the discourse around the league and even the country in the aftermath of his very public exposure of Steelers coach Mike McCarthy's alleged issues and why they drove Rodgers to the point of issuing ultimatums and later detailing just about everything going in the Pittsburgh locker room in a remarkable break from NFL protocol − and Rodgers' long-held belief that matters that swirl about a football team's inner sanctum should remain private. But after 24 hours of pundits, reporters, social media, Rodgers' former teammates and a handful of current ones weighing in, a man with a perspective as unique and, for the most part, as informed as any is about to share his thoughts regarding the shocking meltdown that's occurred in the Steel City. Mike Tomlin, the Steelers' coach for 19 seasons and perhaps the primary reason Rodgers came to Pittsburgh a year ago, is set to discuss what's happened to the Steelers at halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs- Buffalo Bills game in his current as an analyst for NBC. This story will be updated with his thoughts. JARRETT BELL: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers strip each other of graceful endings. Go figure | Opinion What did Aaron Rodgers say about Mike Tomlin? While questioning McCarthy's dedication and efficacy at his job Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers took the opportunity to praise Tomlin anew. Both he and his former coach had long had mutual admiration before teaming up for the 2025 season. But Tomlin stepped down at the end of the campaign, which ended with a resounding loss in the wild-card round to the Houston Texans in Pittsburgh. Per reports, Rodgers was in tears when Tomlin announced the decision to leave his post in the aftermath of the loss. "Leader of men, he knew everybody’s name, knew where they came from," Rodgers said of Tomlin on Wednesday, a comment that also served to distinguish him from McCarthy. "Different mentality." The Baltimore Ravens finally caught a break heading into their road clash with the Houston Texans, as Derrick Henry appears to be trending toward playing on Sunday. Henry, who is in the concussion protocol, was a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday , according to the team’s official injury report . It’s a promising sign for the veteran running back. The 32-year-old landed hard in the end zone after scoring a 15-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter of Baltimore’s 35-33 loss to the Carolina Panthers last Sunday. He initially passed his checks but was later placed in the protocol. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Even so, head coach Jesse Minter sounded confident earlier this week that Henry would be available. “He had a couple of brief symptoms of a concussion right towards the end of that game,” Minter said, via Jamison Hensley. “We do expect him to be back obviously.” Henry will still need to clear the final steps of the protocol before he is officially good to go. Baltimore will need all the help it can get. The Ravens have dropped six straight games , which tied the second-longest losing streak in franchise history, and sit at 4-7 on the season. They have also been without Lamar Jackson, who is sidelined with a thumb injury, forcing Jacoby Brissett into the starting role . Henry has been one of the few bright spots for Baltimore this season. The two-time rushing champion has piled up 793 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns through 11 games. He was productive against the Panthers, too, rushing for 94 yards and a score on 13 carries while adding four catches for 17 yards. The Ravens also got positive news on Zay Flowers, who was upgraded from limited to full on Thursday as he deals with an ankle issue. Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, however, missed practice again with a hamstring injury. Houston, meanwhile, enters the matchup at 4-6 and fresh off a 26-3 rout of the Indianapolis Colts . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australia will soon reveal their squad for the Perth Test against New Zealand. Nathan Lyon is reportedly set to miss out. Recent Sheffield Shield numbers have added fresh pressure on the long-serving veteran's place. End of an era in Australian cricket! 577-wicket legend Nathan Lyon set to be axed from Test squad for New Zealand series Australia's squad for the New Zealand Test series is about to be named, and the biggest talking point is the likely absence of Nathan Lyon. According to a report from Tom Decent of The Sydney Morning Herald , the veteran off-spinner won't find his name on the list for the series opener in Perth. Lyon is 39 now, and his place in the side hasn't been a certainty over the last few series. He was left out of the second Test in South Africa, with Scott Boland picked in his place, which was an early hint that things were shifting. Last summer's Ashes Test in Perth offers a useful clue about how the team management views him at home. Lyon sent down only two overs in that match, because Australia's fast bowlers bowled England out twice inside two days. He then missed the day-night Test at the Gabba that followed. He came back for Adelaide, but a hamstring injury ended his series there, which interrupted a run that had looked untouchable for years. The South Africa tour further added to his misery. In the final Test in Cape Town, his counterpart Simon Harmer won the game for the hosts with 6 for 16 in the second innings and 10 for 120 across the match. Lyon picked up four wickets in the same game, but the contrast with Harmer was hard to miss. After that Cape Town defeat, head coach Andrew McDonald was asked whether Lyon's standing as first-choice spinner would be looked at again. "I don't think it's something to review now," McDonald said. "I think we sit back and we'll go through Shield cricket. Nathan will be preparing for the first Test match in Perth." item.title: California’s Top High School Basketball Forwards, Centers to Watch in 2026-27
item.description: Tarek Fattal California’s high school basketball frontcourt is loaded with size and talent entering the 2026-27 season. The group features nationally ranked prospects, college commits, emerging big men and a pair of seven-footers at St. Francis who could make the Golden Knights one of the state’s toughest teams to handle inside. Class Of 2027 Emmanuel Ahamefule, Archbishop Riordan (PF) — The 6-foot-9 power forward is a nationally ranked prospect in the 2027 class, checking in at No. 129 overall in the Rivals Industry rankings. Ahamefule gives Archbishop Riordan a sizable frontcourt presence, although publicly available statistics from last season are limited. Mahamadou Diop, San Gabriel Academy (C) — Diop is a 6-foot-11 center who has already made his college decision, committing to San Diego State. He earned first-team All-Area honors from the San Gabriel Valley Tribune after his junior season and is ranked among California’s top frontcourt prospects. Cherif Millogo, St. Francis (C) — At 7-foot-5, Millogo is one of the most imposing prospects in the country. He averaged 24.8 points, 11.4 rebounds, 5.1 blocks and 3.8 assists last season, earned second-team MaxPreps Junior All-America honors and signed with Kentucky in November. King Rachal, Notre Dame (SF) — Rachal is a 6-foot-7 wing who signed with Utah State after drawing interest from multiple high-major programs. The Rivals Industry ranks him No. 45 nationally, and he joins a Notre Dame team that also features fellow 2027 standout NaVorro Bowman Jr. Nick Welch, Rolling Hills Prep (PF) — Welch is a 6-foot-9 forward ranked No. 132 nationally in the Rivals Industry rankings. He was identified by the Los Angeles Times as a player ready to take a significant step forward this season. Eteuati-Edwards is a versatile frontcourt player who can contribute as a scorer, rebounder and facilitator. Yann Kamagate, St. Francis (C) — Kamagate has quickly become one of the most highly regarded players in the country, ranking No. 1 nationally in the 2028 Rivals Industry rankings. Jakobi Oware, St. Pius X-St. Matthias Academy (SF) — Oware is a 6-foot-6 wing ranked No. 26 nationally in the 2028 Rivals Industry rankings. He also earned an invitation to the October 2026 USA Basketball Men’s Junior National Team minicamp, another indication of his standing among the country’s rising prospects. Houston Rolle, Sierra Canyon (SF) — Rolle is a 6-foot wing ranked No. 52 nationally in the Rivals Industry rankings. He joins a Sierra Canyon program that annually competes for Southern Section and state championships, giving him a prominent platform to continue developing.

item.title: Bears stun Lions, Eagles rally in NFL Thanksgiving thrillers
item.description: Chicago's Rome Odunze celebrates his game-winning touchdown catch with Bears teammate Kalif Raymond after the team's NFL win over the Detroit Lions (Gregory Shamus) Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thursday as the Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 in an NFL Thanksgiving holiday thriller. Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave the Bears their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions. "We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone." Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Odunze. The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs. The Bears erased an early 10-point deficit, knotting it at 10-10 on Monangai's first touchdown with 4:07 left in the first half. Jared Goff hit Sam LaPorta with an 11-yard scoring pass to push Detroit's lead to 19-10 going into halftime, but Monangai's two-yard TD had the Bears back within two, minutes into the third quarter. The Lions finally appeared to be in control after Gibbs motored 70 yards for a touchdown that gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 remaining. Chicago responded with a three-play, 71-yard drive capped by Williams's 41-yard scoring pass to Odunze. Detroit's next possession ended with a Goff interception, the Lions coming up empty on two straight possessions before the Bears put together their game-winning drive. - Elliott lifts Eagles - In Dallas, the Philadelphia Eagles erased a 21-point third-quarter deficit to beat the Cowboys 39-38. Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining for Philadelphia, who scored 22 points in the fourth quarter. "A lot of adversity, a lot of things we had to battle through," Elliott said. "This team just keeps showing up. Every single week we keep fighting." The Eagles' game-winning drive came after the Cowboys, leading by two, opted to go for it on fourth-and-one with 55 seconds left. Quarterback Dak Prescott was sacked and the Eagles capitalized. Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to DeVonta Smith, and ran for another TD. Prescott threw for 291 yards and two touchdowns, but special teams miscues hurt the Cowboys. The Eagles scored a touchdown off a blocked punt and Dallas kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the final period. The three-game holiday slate concluded with a heavyweight AFC showdown between Patrick Mahomes's Kansas City Chiefs and Josh Allen's Bills in Buffalo. bb/pnb

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket. “Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.” Continue reading...

item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentinos Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
